name: The Lanesborough
positioning: Oetker Collection hotel at Hyde Park Corner in a Regency-era former hospital, with butler service in every room and suite, The Lanesborough Grill and The Lanesborough Club & Spa
best_for: Travelers who want round-the-clock butler service in every room
Families who want a children's program with Hyde Park outings
Spirits lovers drawn to a bar with whiskies and cognacs dating back to 1770

facts.text: The hotel sits at Hyde Park Corner, within easy reach of Buckingham Palace, Harrods, the Victoria and Albert Museum and the Natural History Museum.
The building was rebuilt in 1825 as St George's Hospital by architect William Wilkins, who designed London's National Gallery.
The Regency-era building became a luxury hotel in 1991.
A 2014 restoration involved more than 300 plasterers, embroiderers, crystal specialists and other artisans.
The hotel has been part of the Oetker Collection since 2015.
Rooms and suites are each individually designed with Regency interiors and responsive technology.
The Lanesborough Grill serves modern British dining by Executive Chef Shay Cooper.
The hotel's food and drink venues include the Library Bar, the Garden Room terrace, the Withdrawing Room and The Lanesborough Grill.
The hotel's cigar lounge is The Garden Room.
The spa has saunas, steam rooms, rain showers, a hydrotherapy pool and treatment suites.
The fitness center offers daily small-group classes including HIIT, boxing, TRX conditioning and reformer Pilates.
The hotel runs events including live music, seasonal menus, cigar masterclasses and wine dinners.

highlights.text: Every room and suite has dedicated round-the-clock butler service.
The hotel has a resident Siberian Forest cat named Lilibet, after Queen Elizabeth II.
More than 42,000 gold leaf sheets were used for the gilding on the ceilings.
The Little VIP Club offers family experiences including mocktail-making classes, horseback riding and carriage rides through Hyde Park, and in-room treasure hunts.
The Library Bar is known for its fine whiskies and cognacs, some dating back to 1770.

considerations.text: The Lanesborough Club & Spa is open to members as well as hotel guests.
A selection of ground-floor rooms are wheelchair accessible, with adapted bathrooms and roll-in shower cubicles.
WhataHotel notes the formal atmosphere may feel intimidating for casual guests.
